gnome-bard.name: Gnome Bard
gnome-bard.blurb: Being a bard allows a gnome a wonderful excuse to constantly travel and see new places while simultaneously creating wonderful things. Occasionally, these bards have a reputation for inappropriate or socially critical performances.

abilities.name: Gnomish Shift
abilities.desc:
Trigger The gnome bard would take damage

Effect The gnome bard gains resistance 2 to the triggering damage and teleports to an adjacent space.

abilities.name: Do a Jig!
abilities.desc:
The gnome bard plays a ditty that inspires dance. One creature within 30 feet must make a DC 19 Will saving throw.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target must waste 1 action on its next turn dancing.

Critical Failure The target must waste 2 actions on its next turn dancing.

greater-herexen.name: Greater Herexen
greater-herexen.blurb: When a cleric rebels against their deity and dies in the grip of blasphemous rage, the heresies they committed in life may fuel their transformation into an undead herexen. Herexens seek vengeance against the deity they once worshipped, defiling temples, slaying the faithful, and rallying lesser undead and death cultists to aid them in their unholy quests. Though a herexen's divine gifts have mostly been corrupted into the vileness of undeath, they stubbornly cling to remnants of their former power, still wielding magic and armaments favored by the deity they so greatly despise.

abilities.name: Final Blasphemy
abilities.desc:
When the herexen is destroyed, it explodes in a wave of void energy with the effects of a 3-action Harm spell (DC 18 Fortitude save).

The herexen is destroyed, so it doesn't gain any Hit Points from this use of harm, and it doesn't need to have any harm spells remaining to use this ability

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Heretic's Smite
abilities.desc: While wielding the favored weapon of its former deity (such as a dagger for an ex-Pharasmin herexen), the greater herexen's Strikes deal an additional 2d6 spirit damage to creatures with the holy trait.

kobold-warrior.name: Kobold Warrior
kobold-warrior.blurb: The typical kobold trains in tunnel fighting, learning to use simple weapons that are effective in narrow spaces. Kobolds are capable of landing sneaky strikes against unsuspecting foes, but are just as quick to scamper off to safety when they don't outnumber their enemies by at least two to one.

abilities.name: Scamper
abilities.desc:
Requirements The kobold warrior is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold warrior Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: The kobold warrior deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to off-guard creatures.

irlgaunt.name: Irlgaunt
irlgaunt.blurb: Irlgaunts resemble titanic spiders or crabs, but with cephalopod-like tendrils erupting from the tips of their chitin-armored legs. Their jagged gray shells allow them to blend into the rocky walls of the high mountain passes and deep ravines that serve as their hunting grounds. Despite their size, they move with incredible speed, bounding across chasms and skittering up sheer mountain cliffs in moments. Though they're formidable in melee, irlgaunts have an even more powerful ranged attack. These creatures pelt their opponents with forcefully regurgitated gastroliths—melon-sized clusters of rocks enveloped in coagulated digestive enzymes strong enough to break down flesh and bone. Gastroliths are fragile and explode on contact, spraying the area with shards of rock and caustic acid.

abilities.name: At-Will Spells
abilities.desc: The monster can cast its at-will spells any number of times without using up spell slots.

abilities.name: Regurgitate Gastrolith
abilities.desc: The irlgaunt violently regurgitates a melon-sized clot of brittle stone supernaturally infused with digestive enzymes. The stone and acid explode on impact within a range of 30 feet, dealing 7d6 piercing,7d6 acid damage to creatures in a 20-foot burst (basic DC 33 Reflex save). The irlgaunt can't Regurgitate Gastroliths for 1d4 rounds.

abilities.name: Stone Step
abilities.desc: The irlgaunt ignores difficult terrain composed of rocks and stone.

morlock-tinkerer.name: Morlock Tinkerer
morlock-tinkerer.blurb: Most morlocks have little talent for crafting, but many have an uncanny knack for tinkering. The sounds of machinery and moving parts tend to attract them. These morlocks particularly enjoy the ticking sounds of clockworks. Many tales from Darklands travelers describe morlocks who are able to take used or disabled mechanical traps and restore them, seemingly for the morlock's own satisfaction more than any desire to use the device.
morlock-tinkerer.saveNote: +2 status to all saves vs. disease and poison

abilities.name: Light Blindness
abilities.desc: When first exposed to bright light, the monster is Blinded until the end of its next turn. After this exposure, light doesn't blind the monster again until after it spends 1 hour in darkness. However, as long as the monster is in an area of bright light, it's Dazzled.

abilities.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Disease and Poison
Instinctual Tinker
abilities.desc:
The morlock tinkers with an adjacent construct or mechanical hazard. They attempt a Crafting check against the construct's or hazard's Fortitude DC. The morlock can't succeed if the target's level is more than double the morlock's.

Critical Success The target gains 4d6 healing Hit Points and a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls for 1 minute.

Success The target gains 2d6 healing Hit Points.

Critical Failure The morlock injures itself, taking 2d6 damage (typically bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing, but potentially a different type at the GM's discretion).

Effect: Instinctual Tinker (Critical Success)

abilities.name: Leap Attack
abilities.desc:
The morlock Strides up to twice its Speed, during which it attempts a High Jump or a Long Jump. At any point during its movement, the morlock can make a melee Strike against an enemy in its reach.

The morlock then can't use Leap Attack for 1 round.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: A morlock's Strikes deal an extra 1d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

abilities.name: Swarming Stance
abilities.desc: A morlock can share the same space as another morlock, but no more than two morlocks can occupy the same space. When morlocks share the same space, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls.

norgorberite-poisoner.name: Norgorberite Poisoner
norgorberite-poisoner.src: Pathfinder #160: Assault on Hunting Lodge Seven

abilities.name: Deny Advantage
abilities.desc: The poisoner isn't off-guard to creatures of 11th level or lower that are hidden, undetected, flanking, or using surprise attack.

abilities.name: Nimble Dodge
abilities.desc:
Trigger The poisoner is targeted with a melee or ranged attack by an attacker it can see

Effect The poisoner gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

abilities.name: Impromptu Toxin
abilities.desc:
Cost 1 batch of infused reagents

Effect The poisoner dribbles a few experimental chemicals over a melee weapon. Until the start of their next turn, Strikes with the weapon deal an additional 2d8 poison damage, and targets hit by Strikes with the weapon must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or become Enfeebled 1 or Clumsy 1 (the poisoner's choice) for 1d4 rounds.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: The poisoner deals an additional 3d6 precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

abilities.name: Unbalancing Blow
abilities.desc: Creatures the poisoner hits with a critical hit are Off-Guard against their attacks until the end of their next turn.

abilities.name: Sacrifice Minion
abilities.desc:
Trigger The teaching assistant is adjacent to a minion ally when they're targeted by an attack or an effect that requires a Reflex saving throw

Effect The triggering effect is redirected to target the minion ally.

abilities.name: Necromantic Revitalization
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day

Effect The teaching assistant disperses void energy in a 30-foot emanation. Living creatures in the area take 3d8 void damage (basic DC 22 Fortitude save); willing undead creatures in the area regain an equal amount of Hit Points.

corpseroot.name: Corpseroot
corpseroot.blurb: Corpseroots are rotten, undead trees that grow bright-red poisonous fruit and spread blight to surrounding plants, transforming healthy trees into new corpseroots. These cunning killers drain the life from creatures through their root systems, posing as dead trees until their victims come within reach.

abilities.name: Axe Vulnerability
abilities.desc: The corpseroot takes 10 additional damage from axes.

abilities.name: Blight
abilities.desc:
30 feet. A plant entering or starting its turn in the corpseroot's aura begins to wither and must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or become Sickened 2 (Sickened 4 on a critical failure). A plant that succeeds is temporarily immune for 1 minute.

A plant that stays in the aura for 7 consecutive days must succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save or die. If the plant was a creature or tree, it rises as a corpseroot. The newly risen corpseroot can't create more corpseroots but has all other corpseroot abilities. Plants that are neither magical nor creatures automatically fail saves against blight.

abilities.name: Plant
abilities.desc: When it isn't in danger, the corpseroot spends 1 minute rooting to the earth, becoming planted in place. While the corpseroot is planted and immobile, creatures must actively Seek and succeed at a DC 36 Perception check (DC 40 Perception in forests) to detect the corpseroot's true nature.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Take Root
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per round

Requirements The corpseroot has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect The corpseroot buries its roots into the creature, dealing 1d6+11 piercing damage and draining the target's life force (basic DC 30 Fortitude save). On a failure, the creature is Drained 1 (or increases the value by 1 if already drained), and the corpseroot regains 10 healing HP. If this would make a creature drained 5, the creature dies.

abilities.name: Grab
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.

grimbal.name: Grimbal
grimbal.src: Pathfinder Adventure: Crown of the Kobold King

abilities.name: Site Bound
abilities.desc: A typical ghost can stray only a short distance from where it was killed or the place it haunts. A typical limit is 120 feet. Some ghosts are instead bound to a room, building, item, or creature that was special to it rather than a location.

abilities.name: Rejuvenation
abilities.desc: Restoring Grimbal's head from area F4 to his remains in this room allows him to move on to the afterlife.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Drain Mind
abilities.desc: When Grimbal damages a living creature with his ghostly hand Strike, the ghost gains 5 temporary Hit Points, and the creature must succeed at a DC 24 Will save or become Stupefied 1. Further damage dealt by the ghost increases this stupefied value by 1 on a failed save to a maximum of stupefied 4. Each time a creature affected by drain mind gets a full night's rest, decrease its stupefied value caused by drain mind by 1.

hobkins.name: Hobkins
hobkins.blurb: Hobkins are eerie little creatures, pallid humanoids with enormous, lantern-like eyes and massive ears on a too-big head. Unlike other gremlins, hobkins aren't fully in step with the Universe. Instead, they're trapped halfway between it and the First World—eternally out of phase, just a hair's breadth from reality. They move strangely, with jerking, jittery gestures that jump between too fast and too slow, and they float above the ground. They have a physical form, but they feel off to the touch, with a texture not quite like anything else.

abilities.name: Not Where You Think
abilities.desc:
Trigger A Frightened creature misses the hobkins with a Strike

Requirements There is a creature other than the attacker within 15 feet that would be a valid target for the triggering attack

Effect The hobkins redirects the triggering attack to the required creature. The attacker rerolls the attack against the new target.

abilities.name: Floating
abilities.desc: Hobkins always levitate about an inch off the ground, ignoring difficult terrain unless it would also affect flying creatures. If they're further than an inch off the ground at the end of their turn, they gently fall to that height, without taking damage, unless they have something to hold on to.

abilities.name: Spooky Little Thing
abilities.desc:
Requirements The hobkins is Hidden

Effect The hobkins produces eerie lights and uncanny sounds with no clear source, attempting to Demoralize a foe within 30 feet. Demoralizing this way loses the auditory trait, gains the visual trait, and doesn't cause the hobkins to lose the hidden condition. The hobkins takes no penalty to their check if the target cannot understand their language.

puntzelken.name: Puntzelken
puntzelken.blurb: A puntzelken is a short, stocky creature, roughly the size of an adult dwarf, and resembles nothing so much as an anthropomorphic egg. Puntzelkens are usually encountered near mortal settlements, where they seek out vantage points that offer opportunities to converse with passersby: bridges, fence posts, or walls alongside well-traveled roads. Despite their enthusiasm for social interaction, most puntzelkens come across as condescending and arrogant, seemingly engaging in conversation for the sole purpose of lording their knowledge over others.

abilities.name: Falling Vulnerability
abilities.desc: A puntzelken doubles any damage it takes from falling, before applying its weakness to bludgeoning damage.

abilities.name: Unstable
abilities.desc: A puntzelken takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their DCs against attempts to Reposition, Shove, or Trip them and to their saves against forced movement.

abilities.name: Confident Ramble
abilities.desc:
A puntzelken's unwavering certainty is so strong that they sway the minds of others. The puntzelken spends 1 minute expounding on a topic related to one of their Lore skills, making obviously wrong claims. Any creature that pays attention or engages them in conversation must attempt a DC 22 Will save. Regardless of the outcome, the creature is temporarily immune to Confident Rambles for 1 hour.

Critical Success The creature is unconvinced and gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its saves and DCs against the puntzelken's Deception, Diplomacy, and Intimidation skill actions for 1 hour.

Success The creature is unconvinced.

Failure The creature believes the puntzelken's claims for 1 minute. It can attempt a new saving throw if presented with clear evidence against the puntzelken's claims but can't attempt more than one save per piece of evidence. Failed saving throws don't extend the effect's duration.

Critical Failure As failure, but the duration is 1 hour.

abilities.name: Curse of Fragility
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day

Effect The puntzelken attempts to curse a creature within 60 feet. The target attempts a DC 22 Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature gains the puntzelken's weakness to bludgeoning damage and falling vulnerability for 1 round.

Failure As success, but the effect lasts for 24 hours.

Critical Failure As success, but the effect lasts for 1 week.

abilities.name: Brilliant Wordplay
abilities.desc:
Trigger Mafika is the target of a linguistic effect

Effect Mafika attempts to counteract the effect (counteract modifier +30). If he counteracts the effect, he can use that effect on a new target of his choice within 30 feet.

abilities.name: Tempest-Sun Shielding
abilities.desc:
Mafika transforms unrealized spell energy into a protective shield

Trigger Mafika or an ally within 30 feet takes damage

Effect Mafika expends a prepared spell in a spell slot. He reduces the triggering damage by four times the spell slot's level.

abilities.name: Halcyon Surge
abilities.desc: Mafika casts an arcane spell that takes 2 actions or fewer to Cast, then casts a druid order spell that takes 2 actions or fewer to Cast (paying 1 Focus Point, as normal).

abilities.name: Shift Spell
abilities.desc:
Requirements Mafika has an area spell active with a remaining duration and he is within the spell's range

Effect Mafika moves the spell's area to a new point of origin. The spell's remaining duration is reduced by half. Instantaneous or permanent effects of the spell (such as damage or healing) are unaffected and aren't repeated.

abilities.name: Attack of Opportunity (Special)
abilities.desc:
Urnak gets 1 extra reaction each turn that he can use only to make an Attack of Opportunity.

Trigger A creature within the monster's reach uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using.

Effect The monster attempts a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If the attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, the monster disrupts that action. This Strike doesn't count toward the monster's multiple attack penalty, and its multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

abilities.name: Brutally Disarm
abilities.desc:
Requirements Urnak is wielding a two-handed weapon in both hands

Effect Urnak attempts to Disarm a creature within reach. On a success or critical success, Urnak deals 13 untyped damage of the weapon's type to the Disarmed creature. If he rolls a failure to Disarm, he gets a success instead.

abilities.name: Felling Throw
abilities.desc: Urnak makes a ranged Strike with his greataxe. He has a +25 attack modifier for this Strike and the thrown greataxe's range increment is 40 feet. If he damages a flying creature, it descends 120 feet, possibly falling on the ground.

abilities.name: Ricochet Throw
abilities.desc: When Urnak uses Felling Throw, his greataxe bounces back to him at the end of the action and he can catch it as a free action. If he uses Felling Throw again before the end of his turn (even if it's not at the same target), the attack ignores all cover.

abilities.name: Sweep Aside
abilities.desc: Urnak makes a melee greataxe Strike. If he hits a creature of his size or smaller, he can move it 5 feet in any direction, or 10 feet on a critical hit.

abilities.name: Mantis Ambush
abilities.desc:
Trigger A creature within Yarrika's reach is hit by an ally's melee attack

Effect Yarrika makes a mantis strike against the triggering creature

abilities.name: Occult Strike
abilities.desc:
Trigger Yarrika casts an occult spell

Effect Yarrika makes a fist Strike against a creature within reach.

abilities.name: Grab
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.

abilities.name: Untamed Shift
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day

Effect The Oaksteward's hands transform into wild claws for 1 minute. The Oaksteward gains the following Strike.

Melee 1 claw +7 (agile, finesse), Damage 1d6+2 slashing

hellknight-paravicar.name: Hellknight Paravicar
hellknight-paravicar.blurb: Face covered by a menacing helm and body clad in ornate plate, this figure projects an aura of immutable authority.

abilities.name: Steady Spellcasting
abilities.desc: If a reaction would disrupt the Hellknight paravicar's spellcasting, they can attempt a DC 15 flat check. On a success, the action isn't disrupted.

abilities.name: Universal Obedience
abilities.desc: If the next action the Hellknight paravicar uses is to Cast a sorcerer Spell with the linguistic trait, the spell affects its target as if the target and the Hellknight paravicar shared a common language. The target must have a language.

giant-centipede-bb.name: Giant Centipede (BB)
giant-centipede-bb.src: Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star
giant-centipede-bb.blurb: Centipedes are relatively common arthropods that live, hunt, and scavenge amid dung and detritus. Scurrying about with surprising speed on the scores of legs attached to their long, segmented bodies, centipedes strike with poisoned mandibles.

abilities.name: Giant Centipede Venom
abilities.desc: A target that takes piercing damage from the centipede's mandibles Strike must succeed at a DC 14 Fortitude save or take 1d6 poison damage.

pendidia.name: Pendidia
pendidia.blurb: Naiads protect streams, ponds, springs, and other natural bodies of fresh water. While most naiads lead solitary lives close to their chosen home, sometimes they congregate in coven-like groups where river tributaries meet, performing great magic and blessing the waters of the land. Because naiads' bonds to their bodies of water permit more flexibility, they are the nymphs most likely to interact with humanoids—and even visit their settlements on occasion. Unlike other nymphs, naiads occasionally become adventurers, especially when dark forces seek to despoil nature or otherwise threaten the land, joining forces with others to prevent the corruption of the natural world.

abilities.name: Animal Empathy
abilities.desc: The naiad can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals.

abilities.name: Recharge Spell
abilities.desc:
Cost 1 Mythic Point

Effect Pendidia regains one spell.

abilities.name: Constant Spells
abilities.desc: A constant spell affects the monster without the monster needing to cast it, and its duration is unlimited. If a constant spell gets counteracted, the monster can reactivate it by spending the normal spellcasting actions the spell requires.

abilities.name: Mythic Resilience (Reflex and Will)
abilities.desc: The creature treats its saving throws with the associated save as one degree of success better than it rolled. This is not cumulative with other effects that change their degree of success, like the incapacitation trait (except for rolling a natural 1 or 20). Each time the monster gains mythic resilience, choose one save. The ability should apply to the creature's highest saves first.

abilities.name: Water Dependent
abilities.desc: A naiad is bonded to a spring, pond, or similar-sized water feature. If she is more than 300 feet away from it for 24 hours or more, she gains the weak adjustments until she returns. She can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond herself to a new body of water.

abilities.name: Mythic Power
abilities.desc: The creature has a pool of 3 Mythic Points, and can spend those Mythic Points for any of the actions it has.

abilities.name: Water Healing
abilities.desc: For every 10 minutes a naiad spends soaking in her bonded body of water, she regains 45 healing Hit Points.

lawn-crawfish.name: Lawn Crawfish
lawn-crawfish.src: Pathfinder Adventure: Little Trouble in Big Absalom
lawn-crawfish.blurb: Reefclaws are aquatic monsters that resemble huge shrimp or lobsters. As one might expect from its name, a reefclaw's oversized claws are powerful weapons with their vicelike grip and the ability to inject potent venom into unfortunate prey.

abilities.name: Death Frenzy
abilities.desc:
Trigger The reefclaw is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Effect The reefclaw makes a claw Strike before dying.

abilities.name: Constrict
abilities.desc:
1d6 bludgeoning, basic DC 17 Fortitude save

The monster deals the listed amount of damage to any number of creatures Grabbed or Restrained by it. Each of those creatures can attempt a basic Fortitude save with the listed DC.

abilities.name: Crawfish Venom
abilities.desc:
Saving Throw DC 17 Fortitude save

Maximum Duration 4 rounds

Stage 1 1d6 poison damage and Enfeebled 1 (1 round)

Stage 2 1d6 poison damage and Enfeebled 2 (1 round).

abilities.name: Grab
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a success with a Strike that lists Grab in its damage entry, or it has a creature grabbed using this action.

Effect The monster automatically Grabs the target until the end of the monster's next turn. The creature is grabbed by whichever body part the monster attacked with, and that body part can't be used to Strike creatures until the grab is ended. Using Grab extends the duration of the monster's Grab until the end of its next turn for all creatures grabbed by it. A grabbed creature can use the Escape action to get out of the grab, and the Grab ends for a grabbed creatures if the monster moves away from it.

gunmarshal.name: Gunmarshal
gunmarshal.src: Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powder Keg

abilities.name: Firearms Critical Specialization
abilities.desc: When the gunmarshal makes a critical hit with a firearm, the target must succeed at a DC 18 Fortitude save or be Stunned 1.

abilities.name: Lawbringer
abilities.desc: The gunmarshal marks a foe for judgment, granting the gunmarshal a +10-foot circumstance bonus to Speed when moving toward that creature.

dero-stalker-pfs-4-05.name: Dero Stalker (PFS 4-05)
dero-stalker-pfs-4-05.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #4-05: The Arclord who Never Was
dero-stalker-pfs-4-05.blurb: Dero stalkers are those charged with exploring the surface world by night and seeking out new victims to abduct.

abilities.name: Nimble Dodge
abilities.desc:
Requirements The dero stalker is not Encumbered.

Trigger A creature targets the dero with an attack and the dero can see the attacker.

Effect The dero dodges out of the way, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

abilities.name: Vulnerable to Sunlight
abilities.desc: A dero stalker takes 4 untyped damage for every hour they're exposed to sunlight.

abilities.name: Sneak Attack
abilities.desc: A dero stalker deals 1d6 extra precision damage to Off-Guard creatures.

trained-beastmaster-cultist.name: Trained Beastmaster Cultist
trained-beastmaster-cultist.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #5-15: Cleansing the Flame

abilities.name: Beast Training
abilities.desc: Whenever a beastmaster cultist and one of their animal allies are adjacent to the same foe, they both count as flanking that foe regardless of their actual positions.

abilities.name: Enraging Whistle
abilities.desc:
The beastmaster cultist blows on her divine whistle, riling up the nearby beasts, granting a +1 status bonus to attacks and damage to all allied animals within 60 feet for one round.

Effect: Enraging Whistle

resolved-jamimpi.name: Resolved Jamimpi
resolved-jamimpi.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #5-18: Equal Exchanges-Tapestry of the Mind
resolved-jamimpi.blurb: The opposite of dark nagas in many ways, guardian nagas are benevolent and wise protectors of places of great natural or supernatural significance: ancient oak groves, forgotten holy temples, and vaults of sacred power are just a few examples of locations that these nagas protect. Guardian nagas believe that the beautiful elements of the cosmos are worthy of protection and that devotion to such a grand effort is its own reward. A guardian naga may join a group with similar values, such as a sect of priests or monks, to aid it in its holy endeavors and to exchange knowledge of the heavens.

abilities.name: Guardian Naga Venom
abilities.desc:
Saving Throw DC 33 Fortitude save

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 3d6 poison (1 round)

Stage 2 3d6 poison and Drained 1 (1 round)

origami-mite.name: Origami Mite
origami-mite.src: Pathfinder Society Scenario #6-13: All That Glitters

abilities.name: Flutter
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per round

Effect The paper mite flies up to its speed, and then enters the space of a hostile creature, flitting about its face. The target must make a DC 16 Reflex save. On a failure, the creature becomes Dazzled for 1 round (dazzled for 1 minute on a critical failure).

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Toss
abilities.desc:
Requirements The beheaded's previous action was a horn Strike that dealt damage to its target

Effect The beheaded tosses its head, attempting to move the target creature into another space within reach of its horns. It rolls an Athletics check against the target's Fortitude DC. On a failure, the target remains in place.

abilities.name: Push (10 feet)
abilities.desc:
Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Push in its damage entry

Effect The monster attempts to Shove the creature. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the monster's multiple attack penalty. If Push lists a distance, change the distance the creature is pushed on a success to that distance.

ijda.name: Ijda
ijda.src: Pathfinder Season of Ghosts Hardcover Compilation
ijda.blurb: Ijdas are creatures of forgetfulness. Born from souls who were once enlightened but then renounced it and their role in the cycle of reincarnation, they curse the futility of their existence and find pleasure in leading others to the same fate.

abilities.name: Aura of Forgetfulness
abilities.desc:
30 feet. A creature that begins its turn in the aura finds it difficult to recall memories or to focus on what it's currently attempting to accomplish, and must attempt a DC 21 Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to aura of forgetfulness for 24 hours.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is Slowed 1 until the end of its next turn, as it has trouble remembering what it intended to do and spends extra time on its turn trying to recall what it had planned to do.

Critical Failure As failure, but Slowed 2.

abilities.name: Soul Shred
abilities.desc: Creatures killed by a ijda are difficult to bring back to life or animate as undead. The ijda automatically attempts to counteract any attempt to resurrect or animate any creature that they've killed (counteract modifier +14, counteract rank 3). If the ijda who slew the creature is slain, the creature can be brought back from death or become undead normally.

abilities.name: Manifest False Memories
abilities.desc:
The ijda releases a cloud of red nindoru butterflies from their body, each of which carries a false memory that infects those they brush against. All non-nindoru creatures within 10 feet of the ijda must attempt a DC 21 Will save.

The ijda can't Manifest False Memories for 1d4 rounds.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is Stupefied 1 by the deluge of false memories until the end of its next turn.

Failure The creature is stupefied 1 and Confused until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature is stupefied 1 and confused for 1 minute. It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns to end the effects.

abilities.name: Ruin Wielder
abilities.desc: When a ijda wields a broken non-magical weapon (typically a katana), they don't take any of the disadvantages of the weapon being broken. While the ijda wields it, the weapon becomes a +1 striking weapon that deals an additional 1d6 mental damage on a successful hit.

redcap-cavalry.name: Redcap Cavalry
redcap-cavalry.src: Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm
redcap-cavalry.blurb: Whomever first imagined putting a fey with a bloodsoaked hat on a giant blood-crazed insect certainly had a sense of humor, but that didn't stop the redcaps from trying to domesticate and train giant bloodseekers. Although a flying cavalry was Queen Frilogarma's goal, her court ended up accidentally inventing redcap racing. In this sport, one redcap with a freshly soaked cap is swung around a racetrack by a giant arm while several other redcaps on giant bloodseekers fly after them. The "bait" redcap doesn't usually survive, but they are the center of attention for about two minutes.

abilities.name: Not My Cap!
abilities.desc:
Trigger Their bloodseeker mount fails their blood-crazed flat check

Requirements the redcap is mounted on a giant bloodseeker

Effect The bloodseeker may reroll the flat check.

abilities.name: Red Cap
abilities.desc:
A redcap's woolen hat is dyed with the blood of its victims. If the redcap loses its cap, it no longer benefits from fast healing and takes a –4 status penalty to its damage rolls. It can create a new cap in 10 minutes, but that cap doesn't grant its powers until the redcap has turned it red with Blood Soak. A cap has no benefit for creatures other than the redcap who made it.

Effect: Lost Red Cap

abilities.name: Fast Healing 10
abilities.desc: A monster with this ability regains the given number of Hit Points each round at the beginning of its turn.

abilities.name: Divine Revulsion
abilities.desc:
If a redcap sees a creature brandish a religious symbol of a good deity (which requires an interact action by that creature) or use one to cast a divine spell, the redcap must attempt a DC 21 Will save. It then becomes temporarily immune to all brandished religious symbols for 10 minutes.

Critical Success The redcap is unaffected

Success The redcap is Frightened 2

Failure The redcap gains the Fleeing condition for 1 round and is Frightened 4

abilities.name: Blood Soak
abilities.desc:
The redcap dips its cap in the blood of a slain foe. The foe must have died in the last minute, and the redcap must have helped kill it. The redcap gains a +4 status bonus to damage rolls for 1 minute.

Effect: Blood Soak

abilities.name: Flyby Swing
abilities.desc:
Trigger The recap's bloodseeker mount moves away from a creature within the redcap's reach

Requirements The redcap is mounted on a giant bloodseeker

Effect The redcap Strikes the creature with their scythe.

abilities.name: Web Sense
abilities.desc: The spider has imprecise tremorsense to detect the vibrations of creatures touching its web.

abilities.name: Swarm Mind
abilities.desc: This monster doesn't have a single mind (typically because it's a swarm of smaller creatures), and is immune to mental effects that target only a specific number of creatures. It is still subject to mental effects that affect all creatures in an area.

abilities.name: Cloud of Bristles
abilities.desc: Each enemy in the spider swarm's space takes 4d8 piercing damage with a basic DC 32 Reflex save. A creature that fails its save takes 2d8 persistent piercing damage and is Dazzled for as long as the persistent damage remains.

bog-mummy.name: Bog Mummy
bog-mummy.blurb: The cultural practice of mummifying the dead is not the only way a body can become preserved, nor is it the only route that gives rise to these disease-spreading undead monstrosities.

abilities.name: Tremorsense (Imprecise) 30 feet
abilities.desc: Tremorsense allows a monster to feel the vibrations through a solid surface caused by movement. It is an imprecise sense with a limited range (listed in the ability). Tremorsense functions only if the monster is on the same surface as the subject, and only if the subject is moving along (or burrowing through) the surface.

abilities.name: Breath of the Bog
abilities.desc:
30 feet. A creature that begins its turn within the area feels as if its lungs were filling with water and must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be unable to speak or breathe. The creature can still hold its breath and can attempt a new saving throw at the end of its turn.

A creature that succeeds is temporarily immune to breath of the bog for 24 hours.

abilities.name: Rise Up
abilities.desc:
Trigger A creature walks on top of a bog mummy that lies buried in the mud or peat below

Requirements Initiative has not yet been rolled

Effect The bog mummy automatically notices the creature and Burrows before rolling initiative.

abilities.name: Void Healing
abilities.desc: A creature with void healing draws health from void energy rather than vitality energy. It is damaged by vitality damage and is not healed by vitality healing effects. It does not take void damage, and it is healed by void effects that heal undead.

abilities.name: Bog Rot
abilities.desc:
This affliction can't be reduced below stage 1, nor can the damage from it be healed, until it's successfully treated with Cleanse Affliction or a similar effect; the affliction can then be removed as normal for a disease. A creature killed by bog rot melts into a noxious sludge and can't be resurrected except by a 7th-rank Resurrect ritual or similar magic

Saving Throw DC 21 Fortitude save

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effect (1 minute)

Stage 2 3d6 void damage and Clumsy 1 (1 day)

movanic-deva.name: Movanic Deva
movanic-deva.blurb: Movanic devas are stewards of the flow of good creatures' souls through the cycle of life and death, from the point a creature is born to the day it dies. These angels arise from the souls of stalwart nurturers and protectors, and share a specific connection with a creature's vital essence-its life force. Movanic devas are most concerned with guiding and protecting good creatures during their mortal lives, so once a soul has passed into the River of Souls, the movanic deva leaves its protection to the soul angels, or monadic devas. As part of their stewardship over good creatures, movanic devas can waken within animals a level of sapience to allow them to become kindly and benevolent as well, thus increasing the flow of goodness into the afterlife. They also spend time patrolling the Forge of Creation and the Void, seeking to contain significant threats to life.

abilities.name: Constant Spells
abilities.desc: A constant spell affects the monster without the monster needing to cast it, and its duration is unlimited. If a constant spell gets counteracted, the monster can reactivate it by spending the normal spellcasting actions the spell requires.

abilities.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic
Aura of Vitality
abilities.desc:
20 feet. Allies in the movanic deva's aura gain a +1 status bonus to all saving throws, resistance 10 to vitality and void damage, and are unharmed by the effects of a plane's vitality and void traits. Animals in the aura of 12th level or lower don't attack the movanic deva or the deva's allies unless they are controlled or otherwise forced to attack.

Effect: Aura of Vitality

abilities.name: Dispelling Field
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per day

Effect The movanic deva attempts to unravel unwelcome magic effects on allies within its aura of vitality to protect them from malevolent forces. The movanic deva attempts a counteract check against as many spell effects affecting allies in the area as it wishes with a +19 counteract modifier and a counteract rank of 4, rolling once for the selected effects.

abilities.name: Flaming Armaments
abilities.desc: When a movanic deva wields a weapon, that weapon gains the effect of a Flaming rune.

wolliped.name: Wolliped
wolliped.blurb: Wollipeds are large, docile herd animals found in the snowy foothills of large mountains. Their eight legs give them sure footing even in icy terrain, and they grow thick, warm fleece as protection against the elements.
wolliped.saveNote: +2 circumstance to all saves vs. shove and trip

abilities.name: +2 Circumstance to All Saves vs. Shove and Trip
Ice Stride
abilities.desc: A wolliped isn't impeded by difficult terrain caused by snow or ice, nor does it need to attempt Acrobatics checks to keep from falling on slippery ice.

abilities.name: Regurgitated Wrath
abilities.desc:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The wolliped regurgitates the contents of its stomach and spits them at the target, dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage and 2d6 acid damage. The target attempts a basic DC 20 Reflex save, and on a failure also becomes Sickened 1 (Sickened 2 on a critical failure).

abilities.name: Trample
abilities.desc:
Medium or smaller, hoof, basic DC 20 Reflex save

The monster Strides up to double its Speed and can move through the spaces of creatures of the listed size, Trampling each creature whose space it enters. The monster can attempt to Trample the same creature only once in a single use of Trample. The monster deals the damage of the listed Strike, but trampled creatures can attempt a basic Reflex save at the listed DC (no damage on a critical success, half damage on a success, double damage on a critical failure).
